simple.meaning: חֲפֹר (chăphôr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “a burrower , i.e. probably a rat.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Isaiah, beginning at Isaiah 2:20. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to חֲפֹר (H2661) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: חֲפֹר (chăphôr) / H2661 is traced through Isaiah 2:20 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: a burrower , i.e. probably a rat
definitions.full: H2661. chaphor [ חֲפַרְמָּרָה ] noun feminine mole (as digger ) — only Isa 2:20 , read לַחֲפַרְמָּרוֺת ( מֵּרוֺת לַחְמֹּר ᵑ0 , meaning obscure, see conjectures in Thes Ges Comm. Di).
definitions.rootNote: from 2658 ; a hole ; only in connection with 6512 , which ought rather to be joined as one word, thus חַפַרְפֵּרָה ; by reduplication from 2658 ;

occurrences.englishText: In that day, men shall cast away their idols of silver
